reviews.review: its a fun game I don't think I need to say anything else. I get to make choices that matter unlike other RPG games.

A great conclusion to one of the best game trilogies ever created. Mass effect 3 is a RPG and  third person game in which the choices we make during history shape our destiny. The mass effect 3 plot, which takes place a year after the mass effect 2 plot, begins with a large scale reapers attack on planet earth. From then on, our job is to find a way to stop the reapers and at the same time unite all the galaxy species to make a final attack. But, as in previous games, we have very interesting and important side missions. The gameplay is practically the same as the other games, we can move, run, take cover, jump, shoot, aim, basically what you do in a third person shooter. In this game, melee attacks have been greatly improved, being now very useful in various situations. As in the other games, we have our squad, but it is smaller than the mass effect 2 squad, with characters from previous games and new but charismatic characters. Different from the other games, now, each squadmate has its own powers.  The soundtracks remain epic. Each weapon can now be upgraded to increase damage, ammo, etc. Like in the other games, we can also upgrade Shepard and his squadmates. During the game, we will also encounter characters from the previous games, who end up helping us. On the map of the galaxy, we will have several systems that we can explore to obtain various resources for war. As for dlcs, I just bougth "from ashes", which adds a new mission to the game and a new squadmate. Now the bad part of the game, EMS (Effective Military Strength), or as I called it, the number of the fleet. Basically, in the game, we get soldiers and ships of different species, and all this is translated into a number, and this number will decide your end of the plot. The problem is that the game itself offers little EMS, forcing us to buy DLCS and play multiplayer, which is no big deal. The end we want can only be obtained by dishonest methods. This game deserves a 8.5/10.

Everything you heard about this game is true.
The ending is as bad as you've heard. EA is as bad as you've heard. 

This should have been a good game. A lot of the elements are there. The relationships and decisions you made in the previous games reach their conclusions, and for the most part, it feels pretty right. The characterization remains as strong as you'd expect from Mass Effect. However, there are certain features which are sorely missed, notably the removal of most side quests, and of dialogue wheels when talking with your squad. It seems like a small change at first, but tapping silently on your friends for comments until they soullessly repeat "Hello, Shepard!" to indicate they've run out of quips makes the game that much colder. That being said, a lot of finer moments [spoiler]especially the character deaths [/spoiler] are better than ever, and the Citadel DLC in particular is a far more fitting, intimate farewell to the cast than the game's actual ending. 

But then you kill that last enemy, get to that last cutscene and everything is suddenly the worst. The game spends its final moments drooling exposition about the overarching themes of the series, trying to claim consequences and considerations which have never been presented before. [spoiler]The Reapers kill life to preserve it, just take our word for it? If you destroy them, things will get worse? Synthetic and organic conflict is inevitable and the entire point of existence? Shepard's energy can magically "merge the DNA of synthetic and organic life?" [/spoiler]

[b]And in the end, none of it matters. No matter which big beam of light you walk into, your Renegade/Paragon score doesn't matter, your friends don't matter, your choices don't matter, your war assets don't matter.[/b] [spoiler]The reapers stop, you die, things are great, you un-die for the second time, and then it was all a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bedtime story. Cheers. [/spoiler] To put it simply, the final ten minutes feel completely disconnected from the rest of the series. 

Of course, it wouldn't be Mass Effect without bugs. The UI won't scale past 1080 without mods, hands clip through objects and heads can spin in 360 degrees. You can get trapped on random surfaces, and Ashley won't stop making a clicking noise. Your war assets --the metric of the game's final push, and the thing they keep telling you to focus on-- is kneecapped to 50% if you don't play the multiplayer or the mobile apps, [b]and then rendered completely irrelevant by the game's actual ending.[/b] The game also forces you to run it through Origin, causing further performance issues. It's a complete headache. 

If you want closure on the previous two games like I did, that's the REAL tough choice. You get to send off individual characters properly if you'd like, but the ending makes the game itself nothing more than a big, empty disappointment which retroactively sours the entire experience. I realize that complaining about the ending can seem played-out and neurotic. But the question is: Can you still be happy with the journey you took, knowing that it all led to a choice between three colored lights? For me, the answer is no.

Aside from the FPS issues on EA's Origin App, you'll also have issues with launching the game after a Windows 10 upgrade/update. 

Basically, all issues happening to this game is because of Origin. The problem is, even if you don't want to install Origin, EA ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ makes you otherwise, or you won't be able to play the game. 

Mass Effect 3 is a great game. But because of Origin, you won't get the same satisfaction of playing the game.

Again, EA's Origin app is the issue, always having issues, not the game. 

So Steam or Valve, cut your ties with Origin, they make your company look bad.

A game I very much enjoyed but also with many flaws.

It starts with the need for origin which overlay appearently is the reason for the low FPS you have without this fix:

https://github.com/ME3Tweaks/d3d9-blank-proxy/releases/tag/1.0

Personally I also had a problem with the physic engine and I had to manually download and install this from NIVIDA:

https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/physx/physx-9-19-0218-driver/

Then the game ran flawlessly....with all it little bugs. I found it actually amusing. A lot of little bugs not continously but again and again. Especally in the talks you will experience quite often little bugs in the animation and the pacing and seldom even a little more than a little bug. In the whole game I only experienced one gamebreaker bug which made it impossible to continue but because the automatic saves are set quite often this was again not frustating but actually amusing. If you buy this game be aware that you cant expect a polished game.

The game lives from its world, the story telling and your ability to take influence in it and on the people around you. The missions are just straight forward linear designs and are simple shoot houses were your little 3 man team will again and again slaughter itself through the most dubious impossibilities. Broken up a bit by some minor tactical depth. To not make them to mundane I think every level was different in appearence and got thrown in some minor or sometimes major "specially" for example a new enemy type or an environmental factor you had to pay attention on. This made them enjoyable little trips while I made may way through the story.

The game also has a moral system and together with the sometimes limited answers guides and sometimes forces the opinions you have to express in the game. You either cant resist or get punished by bad moral points which will cripple shepherds face. This is not a dominant factor but still takes influence in some core questions of the game and was something I personally disliked.
Also sometimes things in the story looked very forced in and "unrealistic". This can take for example the form of a emotional disagreement were you just say some words and suddenly people become very supportive which looks very dull. But again something not dominant just another prove how unpolished this game is.

The turian bodyguard is the killer. So and now that I spoilered you the ending we finish this up. If you think you can enjoy to dive into the mass effect universe and want to enjoy a nice story you can take part in and influence it and you can see over it long lists of minor flaws then this game is for you (wait for a sale tough). I enjoyed it. I hope you will too.

This series is lifechanging, and this particular game made me nearly resort to alcohol with how it ripped my heart out and turned it to dust. I keep making the mistake of falling in love with BioWare characters and then letting them walk all over me with their dying or punching me straight (gay) in the face with skewed morals I don't agree with and what not. 

I usually just tell people I like this game series for the hot aliens because I'm way too insecure to tell everyone just how brutally emotionally investing it is; this is the kind of game you really get heated arguing about, it's just that good. 

All I can really say is, play Mass Effect, then play Mass Effect 2, then play Mass Effect 3.

Also, no Shepard without Vakarian.
